question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 20 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The auth feature flag change likely increased latency due to a configuration mismatch.
why_chain: The auth feature flag was changed to 50% in eu-west, affecting the system's behavior.
This change could have introduced a configuration mismatch, leading to increased latency.
The increased latency is observed in the P95 latency metric, which is affected by the auth feature flag.

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused a spike in request volume, increasing latency.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live in eu-west at 02:35 UTC, coinciding with the change point.
The increase in request volume is observed, indicating a sudden surge in traffic.
The increased latency is observed in the P95 latency metric, which is affected by the traffic spike.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of auth v3.26 to us-east was the cause.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment to us-east occurred 200 minutes before the change point, which is too early to be the cause.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to the deployment to us-east.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase occurred after the change point, and the deployment to us-east happened before the change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The data quality issues caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence that the data quality issues were the cause of the increase in latency.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 246 ms (+80%), with a change point at 2026-03-20T02:35:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2132 per 5 min before, 7230 per 5 min after, +239%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.39% before, 0.80% after, +105%).
Changed auth feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (auth, eu-west; 2 min before the change; record R011)
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 02:35 UTC (eu-west; 242 min before the change; record R008)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R012)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R013)
Deployed auth v3.26 to us-east (routine release) (auth, us-east; 200 min before the change; record R010)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (2 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✗ 1 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
✗ Two or more changes fit equally well, so the cause cannot be confirmed.
missing_data: Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Review and revert the auth feature flag change to 50% in eu-west.
Monitor request volume and latency closely during flash sale campaigns and adjust scaling as needed.
Implement a traffic management system to handle sudden spikes in traffic during campaigns.
